also: I’ll be darned if I ever

terms.gloss: may the gods destroy me if …
evidence: Plaut. Mil. 3.2.21: Dī mē perdant, sī bibī (Lewis & Short s.v. enim)
terms.comment: An oath on oneself: what follows sī is what the speaker denies.
Traupman’s phrase, “may it go badly with me if …”, with the future indicative after sī; not found as a phrase in Lewis & Short or the Latinitas loci collections, so Traupman is the only evidence.

phrases.latin: Dī mē perdant, sī ego tuī quicquam abstulī.
phrases.english: May the gods destroy me if I took anything of yours.
I’ll be damned if I know.
I’ll be darned if I ever …

sources: Lewis & Short: perdo
